steps.path: Pages → Home, the top of each room
steps.headline: Each room has All on and All off buttons instead of one switch.
steps.changed: The room's switch became two buttons, as you asked. A button that would do nothing is greyed: in Destin's Room every working light is on, so All on is greyed.
steps.notice: A half-lit room goes fully on or fully off in one press. Lights that are not responding, and lights you hid, are left alone.
steps.risk: A room with only one light shows no buttons, since the light's own tile does the same thing.

steps.path: Pages → Home, the coloured dot on a light that is on
steps.headline: Colour is now a dot of the light's own colour; pressing it opens whites and colours as two rows, the current one ticked.
steps.changed: The "Colour" label is gone: the button is the colour. The picker has a Whites row (warm, neutral, daylight) and a Colours row (eight colours plus a rainbow circle that opens a picker for any colour at all). The chosen one carries a tick.
steps.notice: The dot, the glow behind the bulb, the tile's tint and the brightness bar all change together the moment you pick. A bulb that only does whites shows only the Whites row.
steps.risk: "Any colour" uses your computer's own colour picker, which looks different on each system.

steps.path: Pages → Home, Destin's Room speaker and the TV
steps.headline: The speaker and the TV are tiles too: press to switch on or off, and the speaker's volume is the same thick bar as brightness.
steps.changed: They used the old switch and a thin slider. Now the tile is the power button, the icon lights up when on, the song playing shows under the name, and volume is a thick bar beside a speaker symbol.
steps.notice: Everything on the page now works the same way: press a tile to switch it, drag its bar to adjust.
steps.risk: The TV shows no volume bar while it is off, and some TVs never report a volume Home Assistant can set.
